blocks.title: Gröbner-Shirshov bases for associative algebras and Lie algebras
blocks.content: Gröbner-Shirshov bases for Lie algebras is established by Shirshov [@{[Sh62]}; @{[Sh09]}] for the free Lie algebras (with deg-lex order) in 1962 (see also Bokut [@b72]). In 1976, Bokut [@{[Bok76]}] specialized the approach of Shirshov to associative algebras (see also Bergman [@b]). For commutative polynomials, this is due to Buchberger [@bu65; @bu70].

blocks.title: PBW theorems
blocks.content: There are 8 PBW (Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt) theorems that are proved by using GS bases and Composition-Diamond lemmas.

blocks.title: Lie algebras–associative algebras (Shirshov)
blocks.content:
Let $L=Lie_k(X|S)$ be an arbitrary Lie algebra with generators $X$ and defining relations $S$ and $U(L)=k\langle X|S^{(-)}\rangle$ the universal enveloping associative algebra of $L$. Then

1.  $S$ is a Lie GS basis $\Leftrightarrow$ $S$ is an associative GS basis.

2.  In this case, a linear basis of $U(L)$ is $$\begin{aligned}
    u_1u_2\cdots u_t,\ \ u_1\preceq u_2\preceq\cdots\preceq u_t\ \mbox{
    (lex-order)},\ \  u_i\in Irr(S)\cap ALSW(X).
    \end{aligned}$$

One uses Shirshov factorization theorem: $$u\in X^*,\ \exists! \ u=u_1\cdots u_t,\ \ u_1\preceq \cdots\preceq
u_t,\  u_i\in  AL

blocks.title: Lie algebras–pre-Lie algebras (Segal)
blocks.content:
Pre-Lie algebras are defined by an identity $(x,y,z)=(x,z,y)$, where $(x,y,z)=(xy)z-x(yz)$.

Let $X=\{x_i|i\in I\}$ be a linear basis of the Lie algebra $L$ and $[x_i,x_j]=\sum\alpha_{ij}^tx_t=:\{x_i,x_j\}$ the multiplication table of the linear basis $X$. Then $L$ has a presentation $$L=Lie(x_i,i\in I|[x_i,x_j]=\{x_i,x_j\},\ i,j\in I)=Lie(X|S)$$ and the universal enveloping pre-Lie algebra of $L$ $$U_{\mbox{{\small pre-Lie}}}(L)=\mbox{pre-Lie}(X|S^{(-)}).$$

Then $S^{(-)}$ is a GS basis of $U_{\mbox{{\small pre-Lie}}}(L)$, $L\subset U_{\mbox{{\small pre-Lie}}}(L)$ and $Irr(S)$ is a linear bas

blocks.title: Leibniz algebras–dialgebras (Aymon, Grivel)
blocks.content:
Dialgebra: $a\dashv(b\vdash c)=a\dashv b\dashv c,\ (a\dashv b)\vdash
c=a\vdash b\vdash c,\ a\vdash(b\dashv c)=(a\vdash b)\dashv c$ and $\vdash,\dashv$ associative.

Leibniz identity: $[[a,b],c]=[[a,c],b]+[a,[b,c]]$.

Di-commutator: $[a,b]=a\dashv b-b\vdash a$. $$\begin{aligned}
&&L=Lei(x_i,i\in I|[x_i,x_j]=\{x_i,x_j\},\ i,j\in I),\\
&&U_{Dialg}(L)=D(X|S^{(-)}).
\end{aligned}$$

A GS basis for $U_{Dialg}(L)$ is given by Bokut-Chen-Liu [@{[BCLiu10]}] and then a linear basis for $U_{Dialg}(L)$ by Composition-Diamond lemma for dialgebras which implies $L\subset U_{Dialg}(L)$.

blocks.title: Akivis algebras–non-associative algebras (Shestekov)
blocks.content:
Any nonassociative algebra is an Akivis algebra relative the commutator $[x,y]=xy-yx$ and the associator $(x,y,z)=(xy)z - x(yz)$.

Akivis identity: $[[x,y],z]+[[y,z],x]+[[z,x],y]=(x,y,z)+(z,x,y)+(y,z,x)-(x,z,y)-(y,x,z)-(z,y,x)$. $$\begin{aligned}
&&A=A(x_i,i\in I|[x_i,x_j]=\{x_i,x_j\},\ (x_i,x_j,x_t)=\{x_i,x_j,x_t\},\ i,j,t\in I),\\
&&U(A)=k\{X|S^{(-)}\},\\
&& S^{(-)}=\{[x_i,x_j]=\{x_i,x_j\},\ (x_i,x_j,x_t)=\{x_i,x_j,x_t\},\
i,j,t\in I\}.
\end{aligned}$$

A GS basis of $U(A)$ is given by Chen-Li [@CL] and then $A\subset U(A)$.

blocks.title: Sabinin algebras–modules (Perez-Izquierdo)
blocks.content:
Let $(V,\langle;\rangle)$ be a Sabinin algebra, $$\begin{aligned}
\widetilde{S}(V)&=&T(V)/span\langle xaby-xbay +\sum x_{(1)}\langle
x_{(2)};a,b\rangle y|x,y\in T(V),a,b\in V\rangle\\
&\cong&mod\langle X|I\rangle_{k\langle X\rangle}\ \ \mbox{as }\
k\langle X\rangle\mbox{-modules}
\end{aligned}$$ the universal enveloping module for $V$, where $I=\{xab-xba+\sum
x_{(1)}\langle x_{(2)};a,b\rangle|x\in X^*,a>b, \ a,b\in X\}$.

Then $I$ is a GS basis (Chen-Chen-Zhong [@CCZ]) and then $V\subset \widetilde{S}(V)$.

blocks.title: Dendriform algebras–Rota-Baxter algebras (Chen-Mo, Kolesnikov)
blocks.content:
Rota-Baxter identity: $$\begin{aligned}
P(x)P(y)=P(P(x)y)+P(xP(y)), \forall x,y\in A.
\end{aligned}$$ Dendriform identities: $(x\prec y)\prec z=x\prec(y\prec z+y\succ
z),\ (x\succ y)\prec z=x\succ(y\prec z),\ (x\prec y+x\succ y)\succ
z=x\succ(y\succ z).$ $$\begin{aligned}
D&=&Den(X|x_i\prec x_j=\{x_i\prec x_j\},\  x_i\succ x_j=\{x_i\succ x_j\}, x_i,x_j\in X);\\
U(D)&=&RB(X|x_iP(x_j)=\{x_i\prec x_j\},\  P(x_i)x_j=\{x_i\succ
x_j\}, x_i,x_j\in X).
\end{aligned}$$

Then $D\subset U(D)$, see Chen-Mo [@ChenMo-AMS].

blocks.title: Shirshov's, Cartier's, Cohn's counter examples to PBW for Lie algebras over commutative algebra
blocks.content:
Shirshov [@{[Sh53b]}] 1953 and Cartier [@{[Cartier]}] 1958 give counter examples to PBW for Lie algebras over commutative algebra. Cohn [@{[Cohn63]}] 1963 posts the conjecture: $$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{L}_p&=&Lie_{K}(x_1,x_2,x_3 \ | \ y_3x_3=y_2x_2+y_1x_1),\\
K&=&k[y_1,y_2,y_3|y_i^p=0, i=1,2,3].
\end{aligned}$$ $\mathcal{L}_p$ can not be embedded into its universal enveloping associative algebra.

Bokut-Chen-Chen [@{[BCC11]}] establish GS bases theory for Lie algebras over a commutative algebra. We prove Cohn's conjecture is correct for $p=2,3,5$.

blocks.content:

M. Hall and A.I. Shirshov use constructions and check axioms.

One may use anti-commutative Gröbner-Shirshov bases for a free Lie algebra.

blocks.title: Normal forms for groups and semigroups
Schreier extensions of groups and algebras
blocks.content:
In (Chen [@{[Chen08]}]), it is dealing with a Schreier extension $$1\rightarrow A\rightarrow C\rightarrow B\rightarrow 1$$ of a group $A$ by $B$. M. Hall [@{[H]}] mentioned that for any $B$ it is difficult to find an analogous conditions. Actually this problem was solved in [@{[Chen08]}] using the GS bases technique. As applications there were given above conditions for cyclic and free abelian cases, as well as for the case of HNN-extensions.

The same kind of result was established for Schreier extensions of associative algebras (Chen [@{[Chen09]}]).

Embedding of algebras
